summary.name: File transfer (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia overview of file transfer, the sending of a computer file from one system to another over a communication channel, and the protocols used to do it.
use_cases: learning how files move between computers
choosing a secure way to copy files
understanding legacy dial-up file transfer methods
summary.what_it_does: This Wikipedia article defines file transfer as moving a computer file through a communication channel from one system to another, usually mediated by a protocol. It explains that protocols can carry metadata such as filename, size, timestamp, permissions and attributes. It then lists examples including FTP, SSH File Transfer Protocol, scp, HTTP, peer-to-peer systems such as BitTorrent and Gnutella, mainframe tools such as Connect:Direct and XCOM, instant messenger transfers, USB drive copying, and dial-up modem protocols like XMODEM, YMODEM and ZMODEM. The page is a reference overview rather than a single software product.
notable: Surveys many file transfer protocols across eras, from dial-up modem protocols to peer-to-peer systems
Notes that protocols can send metadata such as permissions and timestamps along with file data
caveats: Describes FTP as older; the page cites a 2012 article questioning whether organizations should retire FTP for security
Overview only; it does not describe a single downloadable tool
